morphology.shape: Spherical, enveloped virion with characteristic club-shaped spike (S) protein projections giving a "crown" appearance on electron microscopy

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human respiratory epithelium; likely originated from an animal (zoonotic) reservoir
habitat.hostAssociation: Infects cells expressing the ACE2 receptor, notably respiratory epithelium
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans; suspected animal reservoirs (e.g. bats) in its zoonotic origin

identificationClues: Diagnosed by nucleic acid amplification testing (RT-PCR) or rapid antigen testing of respiratory specimens
Spike (S) protein binds the ACE2 receptor to mediate cell entry
Multiple variants of concern have emerged with differing transmissibility and immune-evasion properties
mRNA and other vaccine platforms target the spike protein

diseases: COVID-19 — ranging from asymptomatic/mild upper respiratory illness to severe pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and multi-organ complications
Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 ("long COVID") in a subset of patients
clinicalImportance.transmission: Primarily respiratory — via respiratory droplets and aerosols; also possible via contact with contaminated surfaces
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Caused the COVID-19 pandemic declared by WHO in March 2020; widespread vaccination and prior infection have substantially reduced severe disease and mortality in many populations, though the virus continues to circulate and evolve
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: RT-PCR remains the diagnostic gold standard; rapid antigen tests offer faster but generally less sensitive point-of-care detection

examFacts.importantTest: RT-PCR of nasopharyngeal/nasal swab; rapid antigen test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Spike glycoprotein mediates ACE2 receptor binding and is the primary target of current vaccines
